Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

ISt37fi0.1966 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

PROBE, AURAL, JOBSON HORNETS 

PATTERN 

0. FOREWORD 

04 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 25 October 1966, after the draft finalized by the Surgical Instruments 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products 
Division Coimcil. 

0,2 The formulation of Indian Standards on surgical instnmients has been 
taken up on the recommendations of the Advis^iy Committee for Develop- 
ment of Surgical Instruments, Medical Equipment and Hospital Appliances 
of the Ministry of Industry, Government of India. 

0*3 This Indian Standard is one of a series on surgical instruments. 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the mial value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that if the specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

l.l This standard covers the requirements of aural probe, Jobson Horne*s 
pattern used in ENT work. 

2. MATBRIAL 

2.1 The probe shall be made from stainless steel conforming to designation 
SOCrlS of Schedule V of^S ; 1570-1961t. 

S. SHilPBnAND DIMENSIONS 

S.1 The shape and dimensions shall generally conform to Fig. 1. 

^Rults for rounding off numerical values ( nvMl).

4. MANUFACTURE, WORKMANSHIP AND FINUH 

4,1 The probe shall be forged in one piece to give the required shape. 
The loop of the probe shall be round and free from sharp edges. The 
other end shall be made flat and with serrations and shall be capable of 
holding cotton wool. The instrument shall be well balanced on its centre 
line. It shall be passivated and polished bright, free from pits, spots, burrs 
and other surface defects. 

5. HEAT TREATMENT 

5 1 The probe shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 430 to 
90 HV when tested at the tips. 

C MARKING 

€•1 Each probe shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufac- 
turer*s name, initials or trade-mark and country of manufacture. 

6.1.1 The probe may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 

Nom — The use of die ISI Certification Mark is ffoverned by the pr^viflons of the 
Indian Standards Insdtution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Rcyulatioos 
made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with thi^ requuements 
of that standard, underli well-defined system of inspecdon, testing and quality control 
during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated 
by the producer, has the rurther safesuard that the products as actually marketed are 
continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, 
under whidi a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to 
manufiicturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. TESTS 

7,1 nexilillity Teit —The probe shall be fixed in the vice so that 75 mm 
of length protrudes outside the vice. By the application of a force at the 
free end, the probe shall be defiected by 10 mm as measured at the end 
in the horizontal plane. On completion of the test the probe shall show 
no permanent set or damage. The whole test shall be repeated at the 
other end. 

7«2 The probe shall be clamped in the vice in such a manner that the long 
axis of the probe is vertical and the loop is downward. A load of 200 g 
shall bfs suspended through a chord in the loop. The loop shall not show 
any sign of damage or permanent set after the completion of the test. 

7.3 C2orro«loii Recigtance Test — The probe shall be tested for corrosion 
resistance as prescribed in 7,3J. 



ttiS7«»»lM6 

73.1 Copper SulphaU r«rl— The sample thai! be scrubbed with soap and 
vfixm water^ rinsed in hot water, followed by a dip in ethyl alcohol 
( 95 percent ) and dried. The sample shall be completely immersed in 
copper sulphate solution at room temperature for 6 minutes and shall then . 
be washeoi off with fresh water or with wet cotton wool. The copper 
sulphate solution shall be made up as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CuSO|.5HgO ) 4*0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( H,S04 ) ( sp gr 1*84 ) 10*0 g 

Water (H,0) 90-0 ml 

There shall be no red stains or spots on the sample after the test, but the 
polished surface becoming dull may be permitted. 

8« PACKING 

8.1 Each probe shall be wrapped in wax paper and six such pieces shall be 
packed in polyethylene bag or cardboard box.
